title: Myocardial infarction and angina
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's coronary disease, angina or myocardial infarction.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for history of myocardial infarction.

HPI
The patient is a 77-year-old female presenting for a routine follow-up. She experienced a myocardial infarction eight months ago. Since the initial event, the patient reports that the area has healed completely. She currently denies any shortness of breath, palpitations, or discomfort in her chest. She states that she has not required any ongoing specialized care for the event since the initial recovery period. She reports feeling well and maintains her usual activity level.

Review of Systems
The patient denies any recent weight changes, fever, chills, or cough. She denies any syncope or dizziness. She reports no joint pain or localized swelling. She denies any changes in bowel habits or urinary frequency.

Social History
The patient resides in a single-story home with her spouse. She enjoys gardening and walking in her neighborhood. She reports a non-smoking status and drinks caffeine occasionally.

Family History
Her father had a history of coronary artery disease. Her mother had a history of stroke.

Medication List
- Aspirin 81 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40 mg daily

Vitals
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 122/78 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air
Weight: 155 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 5.8%
LDL: 74 mg/dL
Glucose: 95 mg/dL
eGFR: 82 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. She appears in no acute distress. Her skin is warm and dry. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs or gallops. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Extremities show no edema. Capillary refill is less than 2 seconds.

Assessment
The patient is a 77-year-old female who experienced a myocardial infarction 8 months ago. The condition is currently stable and well-healed. She is asymptomatic at this time.

Plan
Continue current medications as prescribed. Patient will continue her current activity levels. Follow up in six months for a routine check.

Electronically signed, 
P. O'Brien, NP
May 14, 2026
explanations: An MI more than 4 weeks ago that needs no further care: old myocardial infarction, I25.2 (no HCC).

distractors.why: After 4 weeks with no ongoing care, the MI is old: I25.2.
